model.rationale: Every available signal points the same way: a D+13 district, a well-funded incumbent, negligible outside spending against him, and markets pricing Carbajal near 97%. With no polls or expert ratings to complicate the picture, the fundamentals-driven double-digit Democratic margin stands.
model.watch: Any late polling showing a single-digit race, or significant Republican outside spending entering the district, would be the first sign the margin is narrower than the fundamentals suggest.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.

overview:
Salud Carbajal seeks another term in a Central Coast district that leans Democratic by thirteen points on recent partisan performance. He enters the general election with a commanding financial position, having raised about $1.65 million and holding $3.4 million on hand, while Republican Bob Smith has raised roughly $200,000 with $47,000 available. No outside groups have invested meaningfully in the race on either side.

No public polls or expert ratings cover the contest, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals, incumbency, and money, all of which favor Carbajal. Prediction markets price his chances near 97 percent. The combined evidence points to a comfortable double-digit win for the incumbent, with the main uncertainty coming from the absence of polling rather than any specific contrary signal.
